claims.text: At 500–700°C under sliding wear, FeNiCrCoCu coating wear resistance is governed by the formation and stability of a protective oxide scale.
The proposed oxide scale is enriched in Cr, Ni, and Cu oxides.
The oxide scale lowers friction and reduces direct metal–metal contact during sliding.
The oxide scale shields the underlying alloy and thereby improves wear performance.
The initial material is an as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu thin-film coating on a conventional metal substrate.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating has a typical multicomponent, nanostructured microstructure.
Oxidizing the coating in air at 600°C for 60 minutes is proposed to promote a continuous, adherent oxide scale before wear testing.
The relevant test regime is sliding wear at 500–700°C.
The hypothesized structural mediator is a uniform, adherent oxide scale that remains intact during thermal exposure and sliding.
The oxide scale physically separates the metallic coating from direct abrasive contact.
Pre-oxidized coatings are predicted to have a significantly lower friction coefficient than as-deposited coatings during high-temperature wear.
Pre-oxidized coatings are predicted to have a significantly lower wear rate or wear volume than as-deposited coatings during high-temperature wear.
Post-test characterization of a successful pre-oxidized coating is predicted to show a continuous, stable oxide layer.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply specifically at 500–700°C under sliding wear.
Applicability outside the stated temperature and loading regime is uncertain.
The alloying elements make formation of a protective oxide scale plausible.
